study.question: Does the small R10 content-preserving linear-summary gain require task conditioning in the content path, the extra rank path, or their interaction, at the same capacity and frozen training exposure?
study.hypothesis: Observed R9 signed-summary replacement harmed quality (0.828197 versus content 0.829197), whereas preserving content and adding P(linear summary) reached 0.829484. R10 linear-copy gain was +0.000450 with private routing and -0.000123 with mean routing, but both C and E routes changed together. Provisional hypothesis: retaining private content and independently task-specific rank-weighted pooling jointly contributes predictive information; the off-diagonal cells should lose some of the diagonal private/private gain in a basis-dependent way. This is a falsifiable explanation of one-seed outcomes, not established complementarity or novelty.

study.proposed_difference: Only separate the score-routing selector used by content C from the selector used by extra E. For raw s[b,l,t], define mean m over tasks with inherited FP32-then-cast arithmetic. C uses s or m according to task_routing; E independently uses s or m according to new architecture-only task_extra_routing. C=sum_l sC*v; E=sum_l sE*basis_l*v; readout=C+P(E). Basis is visible-valid-rank linear or copy. Four off-diagonal standalone modules complete the eight-cell factorial with historical R10 diagonals. Same learnable tensors and same initialization; both mixture branches/pools/P execute in every new cell. All other forward methods remain inherited. When the two selectors match, alias the extra-score tensor to the content-score tensor after executing both mixtures, preserving the R10 shared autograd graph for diagonal diagnostics. No new proposed arm uses that diagonal branch.
